newsitem.title: USA: Diana Corp shares jump on rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Diana Corp shares jump on rights plan.

text.p: Shares of Diana Corp soared in early trading amid fresh speculation about a potential takeover after the company enacted a poison pill.
The shares jumped 2-1/8 to 34-7/8, marking just the latest round of volatility in the stock that has traded between 20 and 120 this summer.
"People are coming to the conclusion that they're erecting a barrier because somebody is about to assault them," said one arbitrageur.
But traders also were skeptical of the company's outlook and did not name any potential bidders.
"They're still trying to figure out what they're doing strategically. It's just a lot of hype to me," said one trader, adding that he was staying away from the stock.
Diana earlier said it has adopted a shareholder rights plan that would be triggered if an investor acquired 15 percent or more of its common stock.

The course of Milwaukee-based Diana is unclear following its announcement Wednesday that it has terminated talks for the possible sale of its APC meat and seafood distribution division. The sale of APC would enable the company to focus on its 95 percent-owned Sattel Communications telecommunications equipment unit.
Also on Wednesday, Diana reported a quarterly loss for its first quarter ended July 20.
